_why: 10 → 14: harness-core's model.mjs re-derives `descriptor`, `DEFAULT_CAP` and `WARN_AT`, which harness-gates' descriptor.mjs and arch-scan.mjs also define. This is the PLUGIN boundary, which — unlike the imagined PATH boundary this gate's IGNORE list once defended — is real: an adopter may install harness-core alone, and a cross-plugin import would resolve only in a checkout of this repository. The copies are small, documented at the point of duplication, and the alternative is a view that crashes for anyone who installed one plugin. Everything that could genuinely be shared in this change WAS shared (render.mjs, and model.mjs itself, which cartography.mjs now consumes instead of deriving rooms() twice).
_why_gitout: 14 → 15: `gitOut` is now defined in harness-core's render.mjs as well as harness-gates' gitscope.mjs. Same plugin boundary as above, and it is real for the same reason — an adopter may install harness-core alone, so a cross-plugin import would resolve only in a checkout of this repository. Note what this change actually did to duplication INSIDE harness-core, which is the part the number hides: serve.mjs and history.mjs each wanted a swallow-the-error git runner and now share one, so the second copy in this plugin was removed rather than added. Do not recover this by importing across the plugins; and do not recover it by renaming one of the two, because the collision is the gate correctly reporting a boundary and a rename would only hide it.
